quotations: At OCP 2026 today, Intel has given Crescent Island a proper name: the Intel GPU D-Series. For the first time, the company also shared a theoretical peak performance target for the chip: 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8. It also disclosed the final memory bandwidth to expect from these AI inference accelerators: 1.5 TB/s. This new information adds to the slow drip of disclosures Intel has made about Crescent Island throughout 2026.

To bring Xe accelerators into the data center, Intel says it’s working with “a broad ecosystem of OEMs, ODMs, neoclouds, independent software vendors, appliance providers, and AI-native companies.” To that end, Intel says customer sampling of GPU D-Series products is in progress, although it didn’t provide any details of a broad launch.
